issues.issue: Standard successors-and-assigns language with no ambiguous term to name; "heirs, executors, administrators" is surplusage between two entities but changes nothing. Nothing here invites construction.

The Agreement contains no assignment clause, so binding effect on "assigns" has nothing to contradict, and it sits comfortably with the sale-cancellation right in 4(b). No conflicting provision found.

"Prevailing party" is undefined and "any dispute ... arising out of, related to or connected with this Agreement" is not confined to litigation, so who prevails on mixed outcomes and whether pre-suit disputes count are both open. A fee application under this sentence would turn on those words.
The fee-shifting sentence is unconnected to any other operative term of the Agreement, which contains no dispute-resolution or venue provision to conflict with it. No inconsistency identified.

The counterparts sentence says the counterparts "shall constitute the entire Agreement" rather than one and the same instrument, borrowing merger language into an execution formality. Whether it operates as an integration clause is a question the words themselves create.

Read with Paragraph 6, which says all negotiations and understandings "are incorporated herein", the phrase "entire Agreement" here duplicates and muddles the instrument's integration treatment. The two sentences point at the same subject from different directions.
A single-purpose execution formality with no term capable of two readings. Nothing to construe.
Nothing elsewhere in the Agreement addresses execution formalities or requires original signatures, so there is no provision to conflict with. None found.

Saying that "all negotiations, considerations, representations and understandings between the parties are incorporated herein" reads as importing prior negotiations into the contract rather than excluding them, the opposite of an ordinary merger clause. A party relying on pre-contract representations could plausibly invoke the sentence as written.

The written-modification requirement sits against a course of dealing continuing past the fixed December 31, 2007 expiry in Paragraph 1, which no writing extends. Whether performance after expiry modified or renewed the Agreement is a question the two provisions leave unresolved together.

The sentence is garbled — "waiver ... of the sume of any other condition" plainly intends "the same or any other condition" — but the intended meaning is recoverable. A minor scrivener's slip that does not alter the anti-waiver effect.
No other provision addresses waiver or forbearance, so there is nothing for this sentence to contradict. None found.

"Gross Income collected from rents and other services" is undefined — "other services" in particular has no boundary — and the clause does not say whether the fee follows income collected after the term ends. The exclusion of "receipts or proceeds from a sale of the Buildings" enumerates one carve-out and leaves other non-rent receipts unaddressed.

The fee base must be read against Paragraph 2(e)'s monthly accounting of receipts and Paragraph 4(b)'s cancellation on sale, and a fee measured on "collected" income raises the question of entitlement after cancellation. Those provisions do not answer it, though none squarely contradicts this one.

"A fee mutually agreed upon" is an agreement to agree with no fallback standard, and the trigger is a general catch-all — "duties not outlined in the Agreement, such as appealing Real Estate Tax Assessments, or other specific requests" — whose reach against the enumerated example is uncertain. Both the trigger and the price are open.

"Duties not outlined in the Agreement" must be measured against the broad duty in Paragraph 2(a) to "perform such other duties that are customarily performed by Managing Agents", which may already capture the extra services for no additional fee. That overlap is a genuine tension between the two texts.
